tasks.short: Develop and introduce a repeatable procedure for identifying advertising needs.

steps.what: Retrieve sales, audience and campaign performance records.
Combine exports and calculate comparable segment and campaign measures.
Discuss commercial priorities, customer gaps and advertising constraints with stakeholders.
Define evidence requirements, advertising triggers, exclusions and escalation criteria.
Draft the procedure, responsibilities, intake questions and review schedule.

loop.input: Approved template, proposed decision criteria and stakeholder requirements.
loop.output: Draft procedure with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check required sections and criterion coverage mechanically; analyst verifies meaning, responsibilities and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass, capped at 6000 generated tokens; unresolved sections return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but stakeholder language and procedural explanations need contextual drafting.

steps.what: Approve the procedure's scope, responsibilities and decision criteria.
Publish the approved procedure in the shared document store.
Set up advertising request fields, assignments and review reminders.
Review pilot feedback and decide which procedure changes are needed.

tasks.design: A reusable kit accepts exports or approved connections from {CRM}, {ADS} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}; deterministic calculations produce a baseline in {BI}. A bounded drafting loop turns agreed criteria into a procedure in {DOCS}, where the marketing manager approves publication. Configure request fields and reminders in {PROJECT}; recommendations create review items without committing advertising spend.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different campaign definitions and disconnected exports made evidence preparation costly. Procedure design also depends on commercial judgement that software cannot settle.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building adapters, calculations and validation checks. Existing approval and template features handle much of the workflow; a bounded model loop assists with prose.
tasks.still_hard: Attribution, sparse segment data and conflicting commercial priorities remain difficult. Connections and metric definitions need maintenance. GDPR and EU AI Act applicability need assessment for the actual use; employee consultation depends on national rules and whether employee data or monitoring enters scope.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when weak demand reflects positioning, product or distribution problems, and challenge an advertising request accordingly.

ambition.what: Monthly advertising-needs review by customer segment

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time rebuilding evidence and writing procedures, and more time testing whether advertising addresses a real commercial gap. With delegated authority, they can initiate segment reviews; budget approval remains with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Recommend budget shifts between customer segments.
reach.learn: Contribution margins, incremental demand and the manager's investment criteria.

reach.task: Identify unmet search intent that deserves campaign investigation.
reach.learn: Query intent, organic coverage and paid-search measurement limits.

evidence.claim: Export integration, fixed metric calculations and configured approvals can support this procedure; this is a proposed design, not a documented marketing case.
Contextual procedure drafting can use a bounded model loop with source checks and analyst review.
A documented government-report failure involving nonexistent citations supports checking generated references before publication.

assumptions: The company has campaign and sales records, but an analyst still combines exports for cross-channel comparison.
Procedure development happens periodically; the monthly review is a proposed extension.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates for this task, not measured results.
The first version uses aggregate commercial data and does not score employees.
Build ranges cover one team's initial procedure and a small set of data sources.
Consent and access includes permissions, privacy assessment and employee consultation where national rules require it; elapsed waiting can exceed the working-day estimate.
unknowns: Which systems, exports and connection permissions are available?
Are campaign identifiers and metric definitions consistent across sources?
Who can approve procedures, activate request templates and delegate review authority?
How many channels, markets and languages must the first version support?
Does the proposed data use include personal data or employee monitoring?
Which national consultation rules and existing employee agreements apply?
research_questions: Which existing approval, template and reporting features can remove custom development?
Which advertising triggers remain useful when attribution is incomplete?
Can a pilot distinguish advertising needs from product, pricing and distribution problems?
new_work: Review generated procedure text against agreed criteria and source material.
Resolve unmatched campaign identifiers and changed source fields.
Investigate missing data and disputed advertising triggers.
Maintain metric definitions, request templates and access permissions.
Collect pilot feedback and propose revisions for approval.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward diagnosing demand gaps and designing useful commercial reviews. Decision rights expand only where the marketing manager delegates review initiation or recommendation authority.
reach: Marketing manager: evidence for segment budget allocation.
Search marketing strategist: unmet intent and channel coverage.
role.ambitious_version: Run a monthly segment opportunity review that identifies whether advertising, positioning, pricing or distribution deserves the next investigation.

job.title: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
